axes.proxy: time-to-first-rule-edit; misread rate on the trace
axes.note: I knew the next floor I wanted, but I initially mistook the ration button's 'ok $650' for a completed purchase and only later confirmed it.

I accepted 'D23 38→0%' to try a safe cash farm for the overnight return, and would make that choice again only when money mattered more than a new floor. Named lapse: The first few town purchases and sends had little room for a defensible alternative.

I can now put a specific threat ahead of the nearest enemy, and the next run actually showed 'hit drain wraith' before those enemies could keep shaving my maximum health. Named lapse: The early editor lock delayed independent row practice, and later changes mixed gear, traits and rows so their individual effects were not always separable.

The Master fight caught me at '6/42 hp' while new carry was at risk, and the final healing recovery made its defeat a relief. Named lapse: Once the mail improved, long ordinary stretches consisted mostly of harmless blocked blows.

axes.proxy: frame time; events per minute at 1x
axes.note: Menu selections answered promptly and big hit numbers were easy to see, but repeated 'REST ✗ NOT SAFE' bubbles kept drawing my eye away from the actual blows; I could not listen to audio.

axes.proxy: death-cause entropy; distinct situations per run
axes.note: The learned 'iron golem · reflects melee' made me keep the reflector tactic for the foundry instead of treating every enemy as another nearest-target fight. Named lapse: Conjurers, their blades and familiar goblin encounters repeated extensively between the new walls.

My adventurer is a guarded rogue who tries an unknown scroll in danger and hunts draining enemies first, with '2/4 rules' sitting above the supplied packages. Named lapse: Early custom rows were locked; most of the eventual priority list remained supplied packages or automatic lessons.

After 'grudge: Ulak the ghoul' marked Jora's killer, I sent Kael with draining enemies first, watched him kill Ulak and the Lich, and saw him survive the Master before reaching D25. Named lapse: Most ordinary report reels were short damage-and-bank summaries without a comparable turn.

axes.proxy: run length; check-in length; dead time at 1x
axes.note: The 'D9–12 swift · 100%' fold cut familiar travel, but later ordinary fights still repeated for minutes; my return visits gave distinct preparation choices while the expanded ledgers took sustained reading.

axes.proxy: share of deaths with a matched-rule trace
axes.note: Jora lost because I left nearest attacks ahead of the draining enemy while healing was empty and 'to corridor vs 3+ · no path ← foes hold the way' ruled out my escape plan. Named lapse: The useful explanation was behind an expanded, long trace; the compact death view did not itself tell me the whole missed escape sequence.
I played alone; 'Ulusk · old hound · served Hale, Iris, Jora' gave the town a continuing name, without another person or a developing conversation. Weight0 under idle-hybrid; award0.
I switched away from the starting fighter to a rogue and later pursued safe cash before depth, even though the town still pointed me toward 'Goal D23'.

The rogue's levels, bigger pack and new floor vocabulary stayed available between heirs, and 'scout · sent 10' meant I no longer had to initiate every expedition myself. Named lapse: Collected set pieces were announced while the report still said set log 0/3, leaving that persistent collection layer unclear.

Torchlit stone, parchment reports and the line 'Slag with silver in it.' made the dungeon inviting to look at, although packed grey figures and oversized control panels sometimes obscured the scene; audio is unassessed. Named lapse: Overlapping grey figures and the large control panel sometimes hid the action beneath labels.

axes.proxy: offline yield vs active; decisions pending on return
axes.note: After four hours I came back to the Lich beaten, an heir lost and 'apprentice · +2 steps → pack 5', so I studied the gas death and changed preparation rather than wishing I had stayed to tap sends. Named lapse: The drill/legacy/forge reward menu repeated across absences even when the underlying expedition history differed.

axes.proxy: share of deaths attributable to a rule the player wrote
axes.note: I credit my extra healing slot for the last 'heal potion · +21 HP' in the Master fight, while the automatic reflector package and personality changes mean I cannot claim every winning blow as my own authored instruction. Named lapse: Automatic personality and reflector changes contributed to wins I could not fully separate from my own rows.

audio: UNASSESSED: agent cannot listen; no audible cues or audio quality awarded.
visualAssessmentLimits: Private-display D3D12 browser at phone400x800,3x; screenshot/DOM observations. No measured frame-rate claim and no claim that an unobserved kill animation was seen.
killCriteriaAssessment: No kill criterion directly observed. Delayed buffered driver/tool delivery had uncertain cause and was excluded, not classified as game input latency or a browser/app freeze. This is a human raw card, not a telemetry claim about unfair-death share or every possible edit.
sameDayRetelling: Jora fell to ghouls after a wraith shaved the maximum health while the exits were blocked. I put draining enemies first and sent Kael with the extra healing and strength my larger pack allowed; Kael killed Jora’s named killer and then the Lich. At the Master the health fell to6, the final heal saved the run, and Kael pushed intoD25 with$3236 already secured.
blindnessViolations: Initial combined read accidentally printed FRAMEWORK sections4–7 beyond permitted1–3. No game source, other cards, QA or coordinator goal inspected.
Prescribed state/text exposes camp navigation not visible in screenshots; attempted PEN and ORDERS selection from those strings before recognizing hidden navigation. No hidden game data API used.

The automatically supplied AGENTS.md operating manual was present in the conversation context; I did not open its HANDOFF/PLAN/CUT references and did not award from its implementation or invariant claims.
highlights: A deliberately safe gas-bank rule produced11 full hauls and a precise recommendation to remove it when I wanted depth again.
The ghoul death exposed a blocked escape and draining foe; the next heir hunted that threat first and killed the named killer.
The Master fight reached6HP before the extra heal paid off, then the run entered a new region.
gripes: Repeated ordinary fights and REST NOT SAFE bubbles made sustained watching drag.
The first ration press only armed an OK confirmation, which I initially read as completion.
Automatic traits, drills and reflector behavior made some winning details harder to credit to one particular choice.
delayedRecallStatus: Intentionally empty; next-day re-ask required. Same-day retelling is separate.
